sections.heading: What is trending: “msft”
paragraphs: “msft” appeared on Google Trends' Trending Now list for US (snapshot taken 2026-11-12T18:54:59+00:00 UTC). Google reports at least 1,000 searches for this term — that figure is a lower bound published in the official Trends feed, not an exact count.

sections.heading: What's behind the spike — the coverage
paragraphs: The Trends feed associates this search spike with 3 news stories from Reuters, WSJ, Yahoo Finance. The headlines, exactly as published:
list: “OpenAI posts steep losses even as quarterly revenue rises to $10 billion, WSJ reports” — Reuters
“Exclusive | OpenAI Continues to Suffer Heavy Losses as Revenue Rises to $10 Billion” — WSJ
“OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time” — Yahoo Finance

sections.heading: Timeline
paragraphs: The trend entry was published to the Google Trends feed at Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:40:00 -0800. Our snapshot was taken at 2026-11-12T18:54:59+00:00 UTC and this briefing was assembled at 2026-11-12T18:56:27+00:00 UTC.

sections.heading: How to read these numbers
paragraphs: Google Trends reports approximate search volume as a lower bound (for example “20K+”). Actual volume can be significantly higher. Trending status reflects acceleration in searches, not the absolute size of a topic. For the full story behind the spike, read the cited coverage below — this briefing intentionally adds no speculation beyond the sourced facts.

faq.a: Google's Trending Now feed links the spike to coverage from Reuters, WSJ, Yahoo Finance. The associated headlines are: “OpenAI posts steep losses even as quarterly revenue rises to $10 billion, WSJ reports” (Reuters); “Exclusive | OpenAI Continues to Suffer Heavy Losses as Revenue Rises to $10 Billion” (WSJ); “OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time” (Yahoo Finance).
Google reports at least 1,000 searches in US as of the feed snapshot. This is a published lower bound, not an exact count.
This snapshot covers US. The same term may trend differently in other regions.
